findings.reason: the deliverable and the done-when must state that the queued repair records the reviewed head alongside the waiver (or the requeue must otherwise preserve it), or the section lands a repair that runs against the wrong revision while its own gate reads green.
findings.text: §17's deliverable records only `allow_unreconciled_runs` in `dispatch_options`, but the queued pointer carries no other launch input: `dispatch()` stores only `dispatch_options` on the queued request (reckon/crew/dispatch.py:958), and `_launch_queued` rebuilds the launch from that dict alone, taking `base=str(options.get("base") or "HEAD")` (reckon/crew/queue_admission.py:143) and reconstructs the node without any base (`_node_from_pointer`, queue_admission.py:74). The repair's base is load-bearing — `dispatch_repair_for_run` passes `base=reviewed_head or "HEAD"` precisely because "the reviewed run is unpromoted here … so the base is always the reviewed head" (recovery_repair_dispatch.py:1003-1013) — so a repair relaunched from the queue is cut at HEAD, not at the reviewed head, and the repair worker no longer has the reviewed run's commits under it. Following §10's single-key options dict makes this permanent, and §17's done-when (launches rather than raising UnreconciledRuns) passes anyway, so the node ships without seeing it.

rubric_items.anchors_resolve: pass — `dispatch_repair_for_run` (reckon/crew/recovery_repair_dispatch.py:501) is the enclosing function of the `unreconciled_override=True` call at line 1005/1020, which carries no `dispatch_options`; `options.get("allow_unreconciled_runs")` sits at reckon/crew/queue_admission.py:147; §10 resolves; and every href in the doc (the landed-evidence archive anchors s2/s3/s8/s9/s11/s12, the-monitor-shows-the-work-it-watches, the-crew-home-has-a-bound, a-window-paces-the-lane, the-local-lane-is-the-default) resolves, the extensionless plan links resolving as `<path>.html`.
rubric_items.done_when: pass — §17's done-when is measurable and carries two controls: a delivered run past the grace queued on a held lane must launch rather than fail UnreconciledRuns, a non-repair node in the same state must still be refused, and the negative control (drop the waiver from dispatch_options) must land the queued repair back in the UnreconciledRuns refusal.
rubric_items.evidence_paths: pass — §17 logs its control under the run directory, the same durable crew run path §9, §10, §11 and §16 use, not a scratchpad or a node-local temporary path.
rubric_items.naming: pass — §17's symbols (`test_a_queued_repair_keeps_its_waiver.py`, `dispatch_options`, `allow_unreconciled_runs`, `UnreconciledRuns`) name mechanisms and code identifiers, with no plan label, stage name, ticket number or changelog prose.
rubric_items.reasoning: a finding — the root cause §17 states is confirmed in the code, and check 3 holds (the caller is `dispatch_repair_for_run`'s own `dispatch()` call, reached whenever a held local-lane repair is queued), but the section's mechanism stops at the waiver while the relaunch rebuilds everything a repair needs from that same dict, so a requeued repair is cut from the wrong base.
rubric_items.single_goal: pass — §17 carries one deliverable: a queued repair records its unreconciled waiver so the admission pass relaunches it with the same exemption.
rubric_items.wiring: pass — §17 declares no ordering and needs none; its write paths (reckon/crew/recovery_repair_dispatch.py and tests/test_a_queued_repair_keeps_its_waiver.py) are claimed by no other section, and the ordering notes on the shared-file pairs (§12/§13 on dispatch.py, §11/§14 on queue_admission.py) are unchanged by it.
